module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1199

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1199](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1199)
- [Hi79] Hindman, Neil, Partitions and sums of integers with repetition.
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1979), 19--32.
- [Ow74] J. Owings, E2494. Amer. Math. Monthly (1974), 902.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Pointwise

namespace Erdos1199

/--
Is it true that in any 2-colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ there exists an infinite set $A$
such that all elements of $A+A$ are the same colour?

A conjecture of Owings [Ow74].
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1199 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (color : ℕ → Fin 2), ∃ (A : Set ℕ),
    A.Infinite ∧ ∀ n ∈ (A+A), ∀ m ∈ (A+A), color n = color m := by
  sorry

/--
Hindman [Hi79] has shown that this is false for 3-colourings.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/HowieHwong/lean-erdos-proofs/blob/b8b641ba2d00dc4d1fe205a078a4159372672459/Erdos/P1199.lean#L85"]
theorem erdos_1199.variants.three :
    ∃ (color : ℕ → Fin 3), ∀ (A : Set ℕ),
    A.Infinite → ∃ n ∈ (A+A), ∃ m ∈ (A+A), color n ≠ color m := by
  sorry

end Erdos1199

sources_consulted: Crossref metadata for Neil Hindman, Partitions and sums of integers with repetition, Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A 27 (1979), 19–32, DOI 10.1016/0097-3165(79)90004-9; including its reference to Owings, Problem E2494.
http://nhindman.us/reprint.html (author bibliography; searched for the cited article)
review.notes: Both declarations faithfully state the cited source. Lean checks confirmed that pointwise A+A includes repeated summands, pairwise colour equality is equivalent to a single common colour, and the three-colour declaration is exactly the negation of the corresponding universal assertion. Empty and singleton witnesses are excluded by A.Infinite; deleting zero preserves an infinite monochromatic-sumset witness. The exact linked external proof compiled successfully and depends only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. The source still records the two-colour question as open and the three-colour case as disproved. Full texts of Hi79 and Ow74 could not be retrieved, but the official problem page and its complete LaTeX statement and remarks were read.
